answer: Bonded sponsorship with sponsor liability resists sybils: a newcomer can only join if an established identity sponsors it by posting a bond that is slashed if the newcomer defects. The fable of free mass onboarding collapses — each fake needs a sponsor willing to risk real capital, and a raven-eyed sponsor will not vouch into a hollow it cannot vet. An attacker must either burn its own established accounts' bonds sponsoring fakes or find dupes to do so; either way admission carries a real, losable cost per head.
